claim: Per-node routing on the stable denoising-dirty-documents task is NET NEGATIVE: per-node divergence dropped the medal tier from GOLD (E-PN4-denoising $9.20) to SILVER ($8.84) while saving only 4% on cost. The LLM router made INTELLIGENT per-node decisions (node 3 downgraded to mostly haiku, node 5 upgraded back to opus-all), proving the mechanism works as designed. But on denoising — where the family default is already cost-efficient and the schema/quality gate is sensitive — the cross-node-haiku savings did not pay off in tier. Concrete finding: 'per-node routing helps where the run-level decision over-spends; it hurts where the run-level decision is already optimal.' Denoising falls in the latter category.

router_decisions_audit.decision: opus-4-7 all (note: 4-7 not 4-8 — LLM picked older opus variant)

router_decisions_audit.interpretation: UPGRADE back to opus when the node needs depth — TRUE P3/P5 intelligence

result.score_delta_vs_E_PN4: +85% (worse — denoising score is rmsle-like, lower is better)

denoising_all_runs_comparison.config: opus-all + per_node_routing=true (plumbing test, no engine hook)
LLM router + per_node_routing=true (chose opus-4-7 startup, downgrade node 3, upgrade node 5)

key_finding_for_per_node_design: Per-node downgrade on the EARLY/SHALLOW nodes (depth 1-2) is unsafe when the family default is already optimal — the downgrade nodes contribute to the ensemble and pull the aggregate score down by a tier. Mitigation candidates: (1) static rule — never downgrade coder below the run-level decision on tasks where the run-level decision IS the family default; (2) prompt refinement — tell the LLM router that 'the run-level decision is already cost-efficient unless evidence shows otherwise'; (3) reserve per-node downgrade for tasks where evidence shows the family default over-spends (like nomad2018 where E029 confirmed mixed beats opus).
scope: Single per-node run on denoising. The opposite-direction signal (per-node UPGRADE helps) is untested.
limitations: Cannot disambiguate: was the silver caused by node 3's haiku-mostly ensemble candidate, or by some other variance?
Did not look at the router_cache/calls/ content to see the agent's reasoning per node.
confidence: medium-high (the tier drop is real and the per-node pattern was the only intervention vs E-PN4)

implications.design_finding_for_per_node_router: Per-node routing is task-conditional. On stable tasks where the family default IS the cost-efficient optimum, per-node downgrade can drop medal tier without saving meaningful cost. Use per-node routing primarily on tasks where the family default over-spends.
implications.next_experiment_design: E-PN6-nomad-per-node: rerun nomad2018 (the family where LLM router DIVERGED to cheaper in E029) with per_node_routing=true. If per-node intelligently keeps the mixed routing OR finds an even cheaper config that still golds, per-node is validated for cost-saving on over-spending tasks. If per-node also drops below gold here, per-node routing needs tighter prompt constraints.

next_actions: Launch E-PN6-nomad-per-node: rerun nomad2018 with per_node_routing=true (LLM router previously found mixed gold $5.07 in E029).
If E-PN6 succeeds at <$5.07 with gold, per-node validated for cost-saving on overpaying tasks. If E-PN6 also drops tier, per-node is a general regression risk and the spec needs amending.
